title: Few-shot Heterogeneous Graph Learning via Cross-domain Knowledge Transfer

problem.claim: Graph few-shot learning addresses label scarcity in graph learning by enabling learning with few annotated examples.

gap.claim: Most graph few-shot learning solutions focus on homogeneous graphs and do not address heterogeneous graphs with multi-typed nodes and edges.

contributions.claim: A heterogeneous graph encoder aggregates neighborhood information from multiple semantic contexts.
A cross-domain meta-learning strategy uses a domain critic to guide adaptation across source and target domains.
An auxiliary self-supervised learning task uses unlabelled source-domain information for cross-domain contrastive regularization during meta-optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present CrossHG-Meta as a novel model for cross-domain few-shot learning over heterogeneous graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three multi-domain heterogeneous graph datasets reportedly show that CrossHG-Meta outperforms various state-of-the-art baselines on multiple cross-domain few-shot node classification tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph few-shot learning targets label scarcity caused by costly and difficult graph data annotation.
Existing solutions largely overlook heterogeneous graphs representing complex systems and domain knowledge.
CrossHG-Meta transfers meta-knowledge from data-rich source heterogeneous graphs to a data-scarce target domain and addresses heterogeneity, domain shifts, and rapid few-shot adaptation.
The model combines multi-context heterogeneous aggregation, domain-critic-guided cross-domain meta-learning, and source-domain self-supervised contrastive regularization.
The authors report favorable results across three multi-domain heterogeneous graph datasets and multiple few-shot node classification tasks.

source_observation.claim: The approach transfers meta-knowledge from data-rich source heterogeneous graphs to improve node classification in a data-scarce target domain.

interpretation.claim: When target-domain labels are scarce, related source domains may provide useful transferable structure if domain differences are explicitly handled.

application.claim: For few-shot heterogeneous graph tasks, consider combining cross-domain meta-learning with mechanisms that model domain shifts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that transfer is beneficial for unrelated source and target domains.

source_observation.claim: The method uses unlabelled source-domain information through an auxiliary self-supervised task and contrastive regularization.

interpretation.claim: Unlabelled data may supplement limited annotations during cross-domain representation learning.

application.claim: In data-scarce graph settings, evaluate whether auxiliary self-supervision can improve node embeddings alongside the primary optimization objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the auxiliary task helps or whether comparable unlabelled target-domain data are required.

unknowns: The identities and characteristics of the three datasets are unspecified.
No quantitative results, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or ablation findings are provided.
The abstract does not describe the domain critic, encoder architecture, or adaptation procedure in implementation detail.
